title: GreenGateway Initialization Answers
description: The answers ggctl init --answers builds a greengateway.dev/v1alpha1 configuration bundle from, in place of the defaults. Every member is an ordinary value: no member can hold a secret value, and nothing ggctl init writes holds one. The deployment profile is not an answer; it is the --profile option. This schema is necessary but not sufficient: the reader in ggctl is authoritative, and it also refuses an operator with topology cluster.

apiVersion.description: Exact document version. No other version, prefix, or spelling is accepted.

name.description: The bundle's metadata.name and its policy's id: a lowercase DNS label. Default greengateway.

topology.description: standalone (default): the bundle supplies its policy and tools documents. cluster: the PostgreSQL policy and tools control planes are their writers, so the bundle leaves both, like Connections, to the server.

operator.description: Generates a policy role named operator, bound to exactly this issuer and these authentication methods, granting admin:config:read and admin:status:read with GET routes for both under the default admin prefix. Standalone topology only. Without it the generated policy has no role at all.

issuer.description: An exact https issuer with no user name, password, query, or fragment (trailing slashes are dropped, as the gateway compares issuers), or the provider:<name> boundary of an authentication provider without an issuer, with the name percent-encoded as the gateway encodes it. At most 1024 bytes.

auth_methods.description: The authentication methods that may activate the role. At least one; none means any method, which ggctl init never generates.
